question: Should `tools.exec.denylist` become a supported persistent exec-security contract with authorized `/elevated full` as its sole bypass?
rationale: The implementation can enforce either policy, but source inspection cannot decide whether STOP rules must be absolute or preserve the existing elevated-full break-glass meaning; that guarantee must be chosen by the security/exec owner.

options.title: Accept documented break-glass
options.body: Adopt the single-owner config contract and retain authorized elevated-full as the explicitly documented bypass after current-head integrated proof is supplied.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Remove the elevated-full bypass so every matching command requires a separate human approval, then align tests, help text, and documentation.

options.title: Do not add the contract
options.body: Decline the persistent denylist surface and continue using the existing deny, allowlist, full, and elevated execution modes.

recommendation.title: Accept documented break-glass
recommendation.body: Adopt the single-owner config contract and retain authorized elevated-full as the explicitly documented bypass after current-head integrated proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to the exec approval and elevated execution security boundary.
